accepted_mechanisms.conclusion: Supported rules have declared syntax types, no essential/DV context, unique mandatory variables occurring exactly once and no private-label/canonical-token collision. Relevant unsupported frames remain recorded, preventing certified nonmembership while permitting independent positive witnesses.

Within the complete supported grammar, closure from local parameter types plus nullary constructors identifies finite inhabited types. Removing rules requiring nonproductive types preserves finite derivations. This statement is conditional on supported grammar coverage, not arbitrary native syntax completeness.

Unique encoded literals preserve original token boundaries. Occurrence-to-floating-order permutation controls emitted child proofs. Basic lexing is suitable for this encoded stream; no observed operator special-case is introduced.

One chosen finite derivation is emitted and structurally replayed against copied frames, exact requested type/tokens and local leaves. Nullary rules preserve prior stack items. Ambiguity need not be fully enumerated when a valid witness is returned; failed conversion/replay remains UNKNOWN.

SyntaxUnknown is not a ValueError subtype. Construction and listed parse/conversion/replay/resource exceptions use UNKNOWN; only completed supported nonmembership becomes ValueError through checker. The future screen must add the explicit catch at construction, ground-guard and per-assertion stages.
